item.title: A Revenue Layer for CKB Nodes (3 posts)
item.description: A second thought on the first question above, whether service income actually brings more full nodes. My “probably yes” was too quick; it’s the real crux. Storage or webhooks can run on any server using someone else’s RPC. So a revenue layer only strengthens CKB if it pays for services where a locally verifying full node is the product, where trusting a third-party RPC would break the service. One example is signing attestations about CKB state, such as “this cell exists at block N,” for a bridge or another chain. item.title: SkillPass: Portable Service Rights on CKB — Looking for Community Feedback (1 posts)
item.description: Yes, exactly — the transfer still happens through a normal CKB transaction. SkillPass is not trying to avoid the Cell transfer. The idea is that the service right is represented by that live Cell, so when Alice transfers it to Bob, the old Cell is consumed and Bob receives the new live Cell. After that, providers check the current live Cell state: Alice → no longer authorized Bob → authorized So the ownership change and the service authorization follow the same on-chain Cell transition.

item.title: Twine: Buy and Sell CKB Without Depositing on an Exchange (Fiber P2P PoC) (1 posts)
item.description: Update: Dispute resolution is now built into the app (PoC) In my previous post, I outlined the concept behind handling disputes: the coordinator reviews the chat logs and uploaded receipt, then either reveals the preimage to settle CKB to the buyer or lets the HTLC expire so CKB returns to the seller. I’ve now integrated that Dispute Desk directly into the Flutter app as a tab for faster testing. Important PoC Note: In this local testnet setup, there is no admin authentication required—anyone connected to the daemon can take a case and resolve it for lab testing. item.description: Reply to Spark Committee — second Pending Thank you xingtian, and thanks to the committee for a genuinely careful second read. Proof-of-possession answers point 2. Mandatory-node access trees answer point 1. Both are in SPEC.md and both are in my “deliberately not promised” list.
